$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $f(x)$ be the $2\pi $-periodic extension of a function from $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ to $x\in R$ with the Fourier series shown above. What is the constant Fourier coefficient of  $f(x)+4?$
questions.worked_solution:
The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is

$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

Recall that if $C$ is a constant, the corresponding Fourier coefficients of $f(x)+C$ are

- ${a}_{0}+2C$  for the constant coefficient,

- ${a}_{n},$ $n\ge 1,$ for the cosine coefficients, and

- ${b}_{n},$ $n\ge 1,$ for the sine coefficients.

In our case, $C=4.$ Therefore, the constant Fourier coefficient of  $f(x)+4$ is ${a}_{0}+8.$

Consider the function $f(x)=7-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ on $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$ Select the correct options below.

in the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x)$ must be zero.
questions.worked_solution:
To check whether $f$ is even or odd, we compare $f(-x)$ and $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =7-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(-x)) \\  & =7-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3x) \\  & =7-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) \\  & =f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)=f(x),$ we have that $f$ is even.

For the Fourier series on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Here, $f(x)$ is even and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)$ is odd, so $f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)$ is odd.

Now, the integral of an odd function over $[-\pi ,\pi ]$ is $0.$ Thus, ${b}_{n}=0$ for all $n\ge 1.$

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is $\text{even}$ and the $\text{sine terms}$ in its Fourier series must be zero.

Consider the function $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ on $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$ Select the correct options below.

$\,$
The function $f(x)$ is
{{field-1}}.

$\,$
Consequently, the 
{{field-2}}
in the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x)$ must be zero.
questions.worked_solution:
To determine whether $f$ is even or odd, we compare $f(-x)$ and $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(-x)) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)=-f(x),$ we have that $f$ is odd.

For Fourier series on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ the cosine coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x,
$$

and the constant coefficient is

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Here, $f(x)$ is odd and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)$ is even, so $f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)$ is odd. Also, $f(x)$ itself is odd.

Now, the integral of an odd function over $[-\pi ,\pi ]$ is $0.$ Thus, ${a}_{n}=0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is $\text{odd}$ and the $\text{cosine terms}$ in its Fourier series must be zero.
